title: matter-tunnel: a portable Matter vendor cluster carrying application-layer authenticated payloads end-to-end
description:
Matter grants every commissioned hub genuine authority over the device it controls — a hub can operate a lock, not merely relay a user's request. Certification verifies that a device conforms to the specification, never that a hub merits that authority.

This is a drop-in Matter component that removes the hub from the device's trust boundary without giving up ecosystem interoperability. A manufacturer-specific cluster carries an opaque bidirectional byte tunnel; an application-layer signing layer authenticates payloads end-to-end in both directions, binding the device's tunnel key to its own Matter Device Attestation Certificate so a relaying hub can neither read nor forge them.

The archive contains the component (lib/tunnel/), the cluster definition and the script that derives an application data model from a stock one (zap/), a thin example application (examples/lock/), the interleaved measurement harness and the raw datasets behind the reported results (measure/), border-router and device tooling (tools/), and device console captures for each claim (evidence/).

Measured results, three transports at n=1000 each, zero errors: application-layer signing costs +40.35 ms end-to-end (95% CI [39.64, 41.07]) over a border router under our own control, and +41.35 ms (95% CI [40.69, 42.00]) through a commercial hub. The two intervals overlap and the first contains the isolated on-device benchmark of 39.9 ms, so signing cost is invariant to the transport carrying it. Decomposing the 103 ms commercial path: a direct BLE link floor of 29 ms (28%), Matter over Thread through our own border router adding 61 ms (59%), and the commercial hub adding 13 ms (13%) — the hub is the small term. On-device cost of the component: +612 bytes of flash for the transport, +19.7 KB flash and +3.8 KB RAM for the complete security layer, on nRF52840.

Ed25519 via Oberon software costs 16.7 ms to sign and 23.2 ms to verify, and beats CryptoCell CC310-accelerated ECDSA P-256 on both operations while saving about 36 KB of flash; enabling CC310 makes Ed25519 unavailable entirely.

Built clean-room against the public Matter specification and SDK. Pinned to nRF Connect SDK v3.4.0 LTS, Zephyr v4.4.0, Matter SDK commit 1206d45da3271670e676f2371670a30154d4429e, and OpenThread commit 0fe68ff23527e8bb9a9821ca96a255fccfbb44a7.
